subject: Performance SLO qualification - p95/p99 (hosted vs current) - postcall recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-25T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO qualification - p95/p99 (hosted vs current) - postcall recap

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today — great to meet the FinLytics team. Quick recap of what we discussed and agreed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Call summary (short):
- Goal: Validate end-to-end p95/p99 latency targets for your inference workload (customer-facing analytics queries with streaming responses) and compare Redwood hosted API performance vs your current provider.
- Key constraints you mentioned: average request size ~ 1.2k tokens input, streaming enabled (token-by-token user experience), concurrency up to 200 concurrent users (burst to 400), sustained throughput ~1.5k requests/min during peak windows.
- Current provider reported baseline: p95 ~ 450 ms end-to-end, p99 ~ 1.2 s (observed on your production traces).
- FinLytics target: p95 <= 250 ms; p99 <= 700 ms for interactive queries (streaming).

Redwood initial assessment:
- Hosted API: we believe we can confidently meet p95 <= 250 ms and p99 <= 700 ms for the majority of your traffic with the following caveats: streaming introduces additional tail variability; we'll instrument streaming end-to-end tests to validate.
- Key levers: connection-level concurrency, request streaming (chunk size / flush frequency), KV/prefix caching for repeated contexts, and batching for non-interactive backfills.

Open items / data we need from you to finalize test plan:
1) Representative traffic profile (CSV or sample traces) showing per-request token counts, inter-arrival times, and percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls.
2) A small set of representative prompts (3-5) and expected average output lengths.
3) Desired test window (ideally a 2-hour window during peak traffic to capture realistic bursting).

Proposed Redwood next steps (we'll own these):
- Share a 1-pager + test plan (attached: redwood-latency-test-plan-v1.xlsx) with test harness, metrics to collect (p50/p95/p99, first-byte latency for stream vs non-stream, throughput, CPU/GPU utilization) and a pre-configured Postman/cURL harness for your infra team.
- Run a staged test with small pilot (10 users) then scale to full concurrency with you on the call.
- Post-test: share raw traces, latency percentiles, and configuration recommendations (batching/quantization/pinning) and a short SLA-readiness checklist.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Samir: share traffic profile + sample prompts by EOD Friday (you said you could).
- Laura: send test plan and coordinate pilot schedule (I will send available slots).
- Marissa/Aditya: stand by to review test configuration and join pilot run.

Thanks — I can be flexible on times next week for the pilot.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - p95/p99 (hosted vs current) - postcall recap

On Thu, Mar 25, 2027 at 3:02 PM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the call earlier today — great to meet the FinLytics team. Quick recap of what we discussed and agreed next steps so everyone is aligned.
> 
> Call summary (short):
> - Goal: Validate end-to-end p95/p99 latency targets for your inference workload (customer-facing analytics queries with streaming responses) and compare Redwood hosted API performance vs your current provider.

Thanks Laura — recap looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The current provider numbers I quoted are 95/99 from our edge proxy (so includes network hop). We also have backend-only (intra-datacenter) p95 ~ 320 ms, p99 ~ 750 ms. The larger numbers I gave are from the full-stack measurement.
- Streaming details: clients open a long-lived HTTP/2 connection; we stream token chunks roughly every 40-60ms for active prompts. UX-critical metric is time-to-first-token and then follow-on token jitter — anything over ~120ms jitter impacts perceived smoothness.
- Concurrency: our critical path for interactive dashboard is ~200 concurrent active streams; batch jobs run off-peak.

I'll upload: (1) sample trace CSV with per-request timings and token counts; (2) two representative prompts and typical outputs; target to drop those into the shared Drive by EOD Friday.

Question: for the hosted run, can you expose first-byte latency for streaming separately from full-response p95/p99? We need both.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Engineering
FinLytics Inc
samir.shah@finlytics.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - p95/p99 (hosted vs current) - postcall recap

Thanks Samir — perfect, that clarifies a lot. Short replies inline and updated plan: 

- Measurement split: yes — we'll report both first-byte latency (TTFB for stream start) and token jitter (inter-token latency distribution) along with standard p50/p95/p99 for full-response completion. We'll add a chart for token inter-arrival jitter.
- Network hops: good to know that your edge numbers include proxy + network. For apples-to-apples we will run two comparisons: (A) full-stack (your edge -> Redwood hosted API) and (B) backend-only (we'll try to replicate your intra-dc path where possible).
- Streaming flush frequency: we'll test with your 40ms/60ms cadence and a slightly higher flush (80ms) to show tradeoffs between smoothness and tail latency.

Pilot schedule options (pick one):
- Option 1: Tue Mar 30, 14:00-16:00 PT (preferred) — 2-hour window during your afternoon peak.
- Option 2: Wed Mar 31, 09:00-11:00 PT — if you'd prefer morning.

Action items (updated):
- Samir/Olivia: upload sample traces + two prompts to the Drive link by EOD Friday.
- Laura: confirm pilot slot and share temporary Redwood test credentials + Postman harness. (I will provision a hosted test endpoint and a small reserved pool to reduce noisy neighbors.)
- Marissa/Aditya: prepare the test harness and join the pilot (Marissa to lead instrumentation; Aditya to run GPU-side metrics).

Deliverables after pilot (within 48 hours):
- Raw traces + percentile tables (p50/p95/p99) for TTFB, inter-token jitter, and full completion.
- Config recommendations (pinning, cache keys, batching thresholds) and an estimate for cost per 1k requests at your profile.

I'll attach the test plan again and a short comparison chart; please flag any missing items. Looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
